title: What If a 25-Meter Rogue Wave Rose Out of a Calm Sea?

scenes.text: What if a wall of water rose from a calm sea? One was measured.
On January 1, 1995, a sensor on the Draupner oil platform recorded a wave of roughly 25 meters.
The sea around it had waves of only six to seven meters.
Then satellites scanned the oceans for three weeks and found ten waves of about 25 meters.
They are not tsunamis. They are ordinary waves that merge and borrow energy from their neighbors.
Giants once dismissed as sailors' legends turned out to be measured fact.

description:
What if a wall of water rose out of an ordinary sea?
In 1995 a North Sea platform measured a wave of roughly 25 meters, and satellites later found ten similar giants in three weeks.
What should we run through next?
